summary: No experiment commits were found since milestone 2026.05.222 activation; the pipeline was inactive this milestone. Both RTX 3090 GPUs remained at 0% utilization with only 4 MB residual allocation each, consistent with no compute-bound work executed. There is no performance data to analyze for this milestone.
bottlenecks_identified: Pipeline inactivity: zero experiments were committed during the milestone window, indicating the conductor either lacked a valid roadmap at activation or no tasks were queued.
Residual GPU memory (4 MB per GPU at 0% utilization) suggests a prior process left handles open without releasing them; this wastes no wall time but is a hygiene gap.
improvements_suggested: Pre-stage research-roadmap-next.yaml before closing the prior milestone so the conductor has a valid roadmap at activation and can begin tasks immediately.
Add a conductor health-check: if no experiment task activates within 15 minutes of milestone start, emit a 'pipeline_idle_alert' artifact and page the operator.
Audit GPU memory residuals after each milestone; add a teardown step that releases any lingering allocations so GPU state starts clean at the next milestone.
Enforce the Pre-Staged Roadmap Convention (CLAUDE.md) more strictly: if research-roadmap-next.yaml is absent or stale at retro time, block milestone archival until it is written.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Pre-stage a valid research-roadmap-next.yaml for 2026.05.223 before archiving this milestone, so the conductor activates immediately without an idle window.
Wire a milestone-idle health-check into the conductor's activation guard that fires a structured alert artifact if no task activates within 15 minutes.
Add GPU teardown to the milestone-close sequence to release residual 4 MB allocations on both GPUs and ensure a clean state for the next milestone's compute-bound tasks.
meta_reflection: A milestone with zero executed experiments is not a failed experiment — it is a planning gap: the conductor had no work to do because no roadmap was ready. The correct meta-lesson is to treat roadmap availability as a pre-condition that must be satisfied before the prior milestone closes, not after the new one opens. Preventing a single future inactive milestone recovers more wall time than any individual experiment optimization.
